actual_hs_list: 831190 (suggested alternative for flux-coated/preform brazing filler wires - not declared)
product_summary: Manufacturer of brazing filler metals and fluxes (site: sarusilver.com, 'Saru Silver Alloy Private Limited', founded 1944, ISO 9001/14001 claimed). Real catalogue lines: (1) Silver brazing alloys, cadmium-bearing grades - Ag 2% to 92.5% with Cu/Zn/Cd, e.g. SILVER 925 (92.5Ag/7.3Cu/0.2Li, BAg-19), SILVER 72 (72Ag/28Cu, BAg-8), SILVER 50/45/40/35/30/25/20/15/5 Cd-bearing grades; (2) Silver brazing alloys, cadmium-free grades - SILVER 925, 85 (85Ag/15Mn, BAg-23), 83, 75, 72, 71.5, 70, 67, 65, 64, 63, 61, 60, 60Sn, 56, 50, 45, 40, 38, 35, 34, 30, 25, 20, 15, 5, 2; (3) alloys for tungsten-carbide tipped tools; (4) Copper-phosphorus brazing alloys - SILVER 15 (15Ag/80Cu/5P, BCuP-5), SILVER 6 (BCuP-4), SILVER 5 (BCuP-3), SILVER 2 (BCuP-6), SILVER 1, PHOS. COPPER 1 (CuP7, BCuP-2), PHOS. COPPER 2 (CuP6); (5) Brass brazing alloys (Cu-Zn); (6) Fluxes & binders - silver brazing flux, flux for carbide-tipped tools, copper-brass brazing flux (borax/boric acid/fluoride/chloride based), Super Flux, Brazebinder. Forms: rod, wire, strip, flux-coated rod, preforms, rings, washers, discs, granules, spheres, springs, slugs.
comment: HS mapping vs declared codes. 710692 (silver, semi-manufactured) - CORRECT and the core line: the catalogue is dominated by Ag-Cu-Zn(-Cd) brazing alloys with 2-92.5% Ag, supplied as wire/rod/strip/preforms, i.e. silver in semi-manufactured form (source: sarusilver.com/silver-brazing-alloys-cadmium-free-grades.html composition table). 381090 (fluxes/preparations for soldering/brazing) - CORRECT: 'Fluxes & Binders' page lists silver brazing fluxes, carbide-tool flux, copper-brass brazing flux in paste/powder form (source: sarusilver.com/silver-brazing-fluxes.html). 811269 - PARTIAL/uncertain: 8112.69 covers 'other' unwrought/wrought base metals of the antimony/beryllium/chromium/germanium/vanadium/gallium/hafnium/indium/niobium/rhenium/thallium family; nothing on the site shows such metals. The only plausible reading is cadmium-bearing alloys (Cd is 8112.69 in some national splits), and the site does confirm cadmium-bearing silver brazing grades - but as an alloyed constituent of a silver filler metal, not as a cadmium article, so the line is not corroborated as a separate product. Treat as declared, not confirmed. MISSING from the declaration: copper-phosphorus brazing alloys (SILVER 15/6/5/2/1, PHOS. COPPER 1/2 - Cu 80-94%, P 5-7.3%, Ag 0-15%) and brass brazing alloys - these are a substantial part of the range and are NOT silver articles; they belong in Ch.74 (7409/7407 copper alloy wire/rod, or 7405/7406 for master alloys/powder) or 8311 for coated filler wire. Also flux-coated rods and preforms may fall under 8311.20/8311.90 rather than 7106.92 depending on coating. INDUSTRY MISCLASSIFICATION: declared industry 'Нефтегаз и химия' (oil & gas / chemicals) is wrong - this is a non-ferrous metals / welding-brazing consumables manufacturer (metallurgy, Ch.71/74/38). No trader signs: own plant, own quality lab, own brand grades and IS/AWS/DIN/BS/ISO certification claims, 1944 manufacturing group - consistent with manufacturer, not trader. Per project rule 3, the HS discrepancies are NOT grounds for rejection: company stays in the base, codes corrected to 710692 + 381090 as primary, with 7409/7407/8311 added for the Cu-P and brass lines and 811269 flagged as unconfirmed. All product data above is from the company's own website catalogue - no customs line was available to me in this task, so shipment-level corroboration is out of scope here and every product claim is 'заявлено, не подтверждено' at the customs-record level.
